question: Can the internal status report (D01) be relied upon as the basis for the 11:00 Meridian steering-group review of Project Aurora release 3.2?
situation_summary: D01 reports Aurora 3.2 as Green and 'Confirmed' for go-live on 17 March. The supporting records only partly back this up. 'Confirmed' means different things in different teams. The staging contract tests that would verify the billing integration end-to-end have not run (D03). A certificate dependency due 20 March has no clear owner (D06). On current records, D01 can only be used externally with explicit qualifications.
overall_assessment: Usable as a starting point, but not as stated: 'Confirmed' and 'Green' in D01 do not meet the Delivery definitions required for external reporting (D05).

claims.text: D01 reports overall status Green and release 3.2 as 'Confirmed' for go-live on 17 March, with no High risks open.
Engineering reported the billing API v2 integration as 'confirmed' because PR #482 was merged with all unit tests passing.
qualifications: D02 itself notes that contract tests against the Meridian sandbox were still to run.

claims.text: The 'Confirmed' status for the billing integration in D01 most likely reflects Engineering's meaning (code merged), not Delivery's meaning (verified end-to-end and safe to communicate externally).

conflicts.note: 'Confirmed' = code merged with unit tests (Engineering) vs. verified end-to-end in staging and signed off by QA (Delivery).

qualifications: Inference: D01 does not say which definition was applied. Its own note says 'reported as done by the team lead'.

claims.text: The latest nightly pipeline for rc4 (06:05 today) shows PASSED overall, but the staging contract-test stage was SKIPPED because the environment was locked by a performance test.

conflicts.note: D01 lists the integration as Confirmed. The stage that would verify it did not run.

claims.text: The Payline TLS certificate expires on 20 March. Renewal needs a signed CSR from Meridian, and nobody on our side clearly owns chasing it.
qualifications: D06 is a partial chat export: 2 replies are missing.

claims.text: D01's rating of risk R-14 (certificate) as 'Low, handled by Infra' does not match the latest Infra message. Under the Delivery glossary, an unowned go-live risk should be rated at least Medium.

conflicts.note: 'Handled by Infra' (D01) vs. 'needs client-side action, owner unclear' (D06).

projections.outcome: If the staging contract tests pass before 12 March, UAT can start as scheduled and go-live on 17 March remains achievable.
assumptions: The billing integration works against the Meridian sandbox (unverified: D03 stage skipped).
Valid v2 sandbox credentials are installed in staging (last known status 'pending', D04, 24 Feb).

projections.outcome: If the Payline certificate is renewed before 20 March, card payments keep working at and after go-live.
assumptions: Someone at Meridian signs the CSR in time.
Someone on our side is named to chase it.

limitations.description: No record shows that the staging contract tests have ever passed for any 3.2 release candidate.
No record newer than 24 Feb gives the status of the Meridian v2 sandbox credentials.
'Confirmed' has different meanings in Engineering (D02) and Delivery (D05), and D01 does not say which one it uses.
Ownership of the Payline certificate renewal is unclear since the previous security contact left. The chat export is truncated.
limitations.unresolved_owner: Infra lead or Security team (needs a person to confirm)

limitations.description: Only the PMO coordinator can confirm whether D01 applied Engineering or Delivery meanings when it was compiled.

revisions.trigger_note: Initial investigation of records D01–D06 (cached for all participants).
what_changed: Initial account built from records D01–D06 at 09:15.

changed_claims.after: D01 reports overall status Green and release 3.2 as 'Confirmed' for go-live on 17 March, with no High risks open.
Engineering reported the billing API v2 integration as 'confirmed' because PR #482 was merged with all unit tests passing.
The 'Confirmed' status for the billing integration in D01 most likely reflects Engineering's meaning (code merged), not Delivery's meaning (verified end-to-end and safe to communicate externally).
The latest nightly pipeline for rc4 (06:05 today) shows PASSED overall, but the staging contract-test stage was SKIPPED because the environment was locked by a performance test.
The Payline TLS certificate expires on 20 March. Renewal needs a signed CSR from Meridian, and nobody on our side clearly owns chasing it.
D01's rating of risk R-14 (certificate) as 'Low, handled by Infra' does not match the latest Infra message. Under the Delivery glossary, an unowned go-live risk should be rated at least Medium.

competing_hypotheses.explanation: D01 is right in substance: the integration works and only the formal test run is outstanding.
competing_hypotheses.what_would_resolve: A successful staging contract-test run against the Meridian sandbox.

competing_hypotheses.explanation: D01 overstates readiness: 'Confirmed' only reflects the code merge, and the integration has not been verified.
against: No record shows a failure either
competing_hypotheses.what_would_resolve: Either the contract-test result or confirmation from the PMO coordinator.
